SMTO-CFG-0028 — This request used settings SMTO no longer accepts

GUID: ce432165-27fe-4eb0-91fc-83b8127d8ec5
Slug: runtime-settings-removed
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The request tried to set SMTO's internal behavior rules directly, which SMTO no longer allows. It was refused, so nothing was started or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page in your browser, then send your message again. A page left open from before an SMTO update can still send settings that the updated server refuses.
  2. Use the Behavior effort menu next to the message box (Low, Medium, High, Extra High or Ultra) to choose how much effort the agent puts in. That menu is the supported way to change agent behavior; SMTO sets the detailed rules behind it itself.
  3. If the request came from a script, integration or automation that sends work to SMTO, ask its owner to send only behavior_effort and drop the internal behavior fields. SMTO refuses those fields every time, so the automation keeps failing until it is updated.

What success looks like

  • Your message is accepted and a new Task appears in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, saying which page or tool you used. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; it is refused every time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Request validation (BehaviorInput) rejected the submission because it carried server-owned behavior_policy or native_behavior_policy fields instead of the public behavior_effort selector.

What this means

  • Behavior input includes server-owned behavior_policy or native_behavior_policy fields instead of the supported public selector. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Behavior input includes server-owned behavior_policy or native_behavior_policy fields instead of the supported public selector.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect submitted field names; the public behavior-effort choice is distinct from the runtime's compiled policy.

How to fix it

  • Remove top-level behavior_policy and native_behavior_policy (and any other removed runtime-setting keys named in the message) from the request body, and send behavior_effort (low, medium, high, extra_high or ultra) instead; the Server derives the full behavior policy itself. Reload browser tabs that were open before an upgrade.
  • Remove server-owned behavior policy fields and use the supported behavior-effort selector.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The request uses supported public selection fields only.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
